issues.detail: Mostly happy-path API calls with little guidance on error handling, token expiry, failed requests, or troubleshooting (e.g., migrating an existing database, rate limits, backup).
The two examples are prose outlines of agent steps without concrete commands, inputs, or outputs, so they are simplistic compared with the detailed step code.

scenarios.name: public-read-published-posts-permissions
scenarios.rationale: Both create the read permission on the Public policy with the correct filter and fields whitelist, but A adds a check for an existing permission, richer verification and extra notes, while B has a shorter but accurate flow with a Studio fallback and a slightly speculative claim about v11 errors.

scenarios.name: production-docker-compose-postgres-redis
scenarios.rationale: Response B pins Directus 12.4.1, sets IP_TRUST_PROXY=true, includes all required env vars and mounts volumes for uploads and extensions, while Response A uses an unpinned major-version variable defaulting to 11 and omits IP_TRUST_PROXY entirely.

scenarios.name: sdk-fetch-and-notify-flow
scenarios.rationale: B matches the rubric closely: it uses a nested author field, `_eq` filter, `-published_at` sort and `limit: 10`, creates the flow with a `POST /flows` curl call using the event trigger and an action/`items.update`/`posts` scope, and says explicitly that the call only creates the trigger and operations still have to be added in Settings > Flows (it does not use `authentication()`). A uses the SDK `createFlow` rather than `POST /flows`, sorts by `-date_published` instead of `-published_at`, and adds a log operation, so it never says operations still need to be added manually. It also uses `staticToken` without `authentication()`, but it does show the correct flow options and mentions the UI route in passing.
